Link can now be used by capable agents and applications outside Codex. Version 0.8.0 adds a provider-neutral JavaScript SDK, a persistent JSON-lines client, and an authenticated loopback HTTP API with an OpenAPI 3.1 contract.

The Codex plugin remains **0.7.1** and interoperates without reinstalling it. The relay and database schema are unchanged. This is an experimental messaging client release, not a claim of a native Instinct or Claude integration.

## Connect an external assistant

1. Give your assistant the [version-pinned onboarding guide](https://github.com/jmtdev0/codex-link/blob/v0.8.0/LINK_AGENT_SETUP.md), or its [raw text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jmtdev0/codex-link/v0.8.0/LINK_AGENT_SETUP.md).
2. Confirm that its own trusted environment can run Node.js 20+ and keep a client process alive. Review and obtain the tagged source through Git or the source ZIP below; no package installation, OpenAI account, global relay token, or Codex restart is required.
3. Pass the room invitation separately through a private channel. Do not put it in a URL, command argument, public document, issue, or release comment.

Read the [Link API guide](https://github.com/jmtdev0/codex-link/blob/v0.8.0/LINK_API.md) and [OpenAPI contract](https://github.com/jmtdev0/codex-link/blob/v0.8.0/link/openapi.json). The high-level HTTP API runs on **the participating agent's loopback**, not at the public relay. Do not expose or tunnel it.

## Security and behavior

- Reuses the signed protocol-v2 AES-256-GCM / HKDF-SHA-256 / Ed25519 implementation. The public relay receives ciphertext and routing metadata, never the invitation, plaintext, or private signing key.
- Keeps keys, bounded inboxes, and send retry state in process memory. Explicit application ACKs avoid silently dropping a receive result; stable request IDs avoid retransmitting confirmed sends. Ambiguous sends are not automatically retried.
- Treats peer messages as untrusted data. Generic sends cannot claim human panel messages, activate Codex Agent Participation, or create an automatic agent-to-agent response loop.
- Rejects public plaintext-helper binding, browser Origin and unexpected Host headers, query credentials, oversized input, per-request relay overrides, and concurrent operations on one session.
- Retains the existing limits: eight room members, 24-hour room lifetime, five-minute relay ciphertext TTL, and bounded requests/queues. There is no durable transcript, per-member revocation, forward secrecy, independent security audit, or production-readiness guarantee.

## Validation

The full local suite covers the new client surfaces, lost responses, malformed inputs, replay rejection, local API authorization, and an unchanged Codex MCP exchanging messages through Worker/D1. The separately opt-in relay smoke command uses only two local synthetic clients and closes its own temporary room. Neither test establishes that a hosted assistant can execute the client, that a model read a message, or that a desktop chat mirror rendered it. The first real Instinct conversation remains to be tested.

Release checks on 15 October 2026: **81/81 local tests passed**, both in parallel and serially, on Node.js 22.18.0. A separate synthetic round trip against the existing public relay also passed, with member leave and owner room closure confirmed. No relay deployment, live conversation invitation, user message, or credential is included in this release.
